claim: Skype 5.0 for Windows released Oct 14, 2010 with Facebook News Feed integration, group video calling beta, call recovery, revitalized UI/home dashboard
Skype 5.0 added automatic call recovery for calls interrupted by internet problems
Skype 5.0 gave a free trial of group video calling
Group video calling launched as paid premium service Jan 2011, $4.99/day or $8.99/month, in Skype 5.1 Windows business version
Group video calling allowed 3-10 people for businesses
Skype 5.2 for Mac (Jul 5 2011) added group screen sharing, call control bar, Recents section
Group video/screen sharing required Skype Premium $4.49-$8.99/month, $4.99 day pass
Skype 5.5 for Windows released mid-2011 with deep Facebook integration
Skype 5.11 Windows Beta (Sep 14 2012) tightened Facebook/Microsoft account integration
Skype 5.10.0.116 stable Windows build; 5.11 Beta allowed Microsoft/Facebook login
Group video calling made completely free April 2014 across Windows/Mac/Xbox One
Skype 5.0 Facebook Connect login shows News Feed, mood-message sync, comment/like
Skype 5.0 lets users call/SMS Facebook friends' phones and free Skype-to-Skype calls to Facebook contacts using Skype
Skype 5.0 automatic call recovery
Skype 5.0 free trial of group video calling
Skype 5.0 improved UI and new home dashboard with mood feed and tutorials
Group video calling supports 10 concurrent video streams shown as ten screens
Call Quality information button dialog during calls
Full screen Skype window title bar cannot be dragged
Skype Options grouped into Privacy, Notifications, Sounds, Hotkeys, Connection, Advanced
Privacy options reached via Tools>Options>Privacy>Blocked Contacts
Skype 5.0 beta group video chat up to 9 other people (10 total)
Skype 5.0 lets users interact with Facebook news feed (post/comment/like) from Skype
Skype 5.0 contact search screen features images, mood messages, real-time results
Skype 5.5 added hidden emoticons: facepalm/fail, wfh, fingers/yn, tumbleweed, lalala/notlistening, waiting/impatience, highfive/h5
Skype 5.5 hidden emoticons list notes 2 more Easter egg emoticons
Skype 5.0 beta (May 14 2010) supported group video calling up to 5 people
Group calling planned as paid premium feature rolling out in 2010, free during 5.0 preview
Skype 5.2 for Mac added group screen sharing upgrading from one-to-one only
Skype 5.2 group video/screen sharing requires Premium $4.49-$8.99/month
Skype 5.5 for Windows rolled out around same time as 5.2 Mac with deep Facebook integration
Skype 5.0 had screen-sharing issues: cropping on resize, high-res hardware problems, incompatibility with Mac 2.8 screen sharing
Skype 5.0 call quality indicator sometimes incorrectly reported medium quality during HD call
Skype 5.5.117 optimized for Windows 8; 5.3 incompatible/crashed on Windows 8
Group video calling eventually made free for everyone on Windows, Mac, Xbox One
SkypeOut requires purchasing Skype Credit in advance for per-minute calling to landlines/mobiles
